title: "Ventilation design as disease control"

Research Assistant, Institute of Architecture and Technology, Royal Danish
Academy, Copenhagen, 2021–2022.

Airflow and thermal conditions in experimental solar housing, modelled as
mesh-based RANS CFD in OpenFOAM and ANSYS Fluent. The design objective was not
comfort alone: ventilation was the intervention being tested for mosquito
control, so the model had to hold up as a health claim and not only as a physics
result. That constraint is what pushed the work from simulation into measurement.

## Measuring the thing you modelled

I assembled Internet-of-Things sensor units, deployed them on site in Tanzania,
and monitored them remotely from Copenhagen over a six-month campaign. Model
output was validated against measured Physiological Equivalent Temperature and
Universal Thermal Climate Index. Four low-cost particulate units built for the
same programme outperformed the commercial instruments they were checked against.

## Why it still matters to me

This was the first time a microclimate model I built was answerable to an
outcome measured in people rather than in pascals. Everything since — the
mesoscale-to-microscale chain, the insistence on a validation record travelling
with the model — comes from that.
